priors.claim: Generic participation-weighted relative forecast scoring constitutes a novel PFL mechanism

priors.limit: Modern GJ Open is distinct from GJP Year1 rules, does not solve logged person-question opportunity or causal leaderboard design. Comparators must match exact scoring and estimand.

priors.claim: A visible leaderboard alone produces a positive and durable causal effect on participation
priors.support: Palikot, Agrawal, Kanodia and Athey (2026) randomized ~10,000 pupils in 138 schools: contest treatment included dedicated leaderboard, book prizes for top 1,000, in-app alerts and WhatsApp parent notifications; controls retained standard leaderboard. Authors report +0.96 stories (SE0.32) during contest and +0.301 (SE0.139) after 12 weeks.
priors.limits: Causal effect belongs to bundled contest intervention in education, not isolated leaderboard or adult political forecast decisions. No person-level data inspected.

additional_verified_20261029.design: 138 randomized schools, 9327 actually randomized students (figure 1 original paper); 50% assigned at school level
additional_verified_20261029.important_timing: 4-week active 9.6% treatment vs6.5% control; 12-week active 14.3% vs12.2%. Twelve-week story ITT +0.301 SE0.139 over control mean0.395 is NOT the same four-week participation window.
additional_verified_20261029.data_rights: Official publisher section says 'Data will be provided in supplementary information files'; underlying person data not accessed.
additional_verified_20261029.mechanism: Bundled trial school-wide contest + leaderboard + books + notifications; conditional-on-rank analyses posttreatment noncausal; active-user mean decomposition conditional only.

priors.claim: More performance feedback universally increases contest entry
priors.support: Erat, Somasundaram and Stouras 2026 working paper reports 511 subjects, 73 contests, 32 rounds each and 16,352 entry decisions; salient feedback lowers excessive entry relative to efficient benchmark under their treatments. Author webpage links OSF Data & Code and AsPredicted preregistration.
priors.limits: Working paper under review; no independent reproduction, OSF page inaccessible through current search and individual files/license not verified. Treatment feedback on earnings, not PFL public ranking; average fewer entries may improve welfare under excessive entry.

priors.claim: Public report of 2,246 GJP participants proves an assigned nonresponse-complete accessible treatment roster
priors.support: Association for Psychological Science 2014 description of Mellers year1 reports starting 2,246 participants and randomization 3 × 4; cannot infer each assigned user_id and entry time from that aggregate count.
priors.limits: Original Dataverse DDI contains forecast event rows and field labels, not confirmed roster with zero-forecasters. No human bytes downloaded.

priors.claim: Independent material suitable for sequential contest alternatives has no discoverable dataset
priors.support: Nelson & Ryvkin (2024) Mendeley Data DOI 10.17632/n6t49bxhh4.3 reports CC BY4, published experimental instructions, Stata files and code for four sequential-contest treatments.
priors.limits: Separate sequential-contest question, not verified leaderboard visibility; no data downloaded, personal-data processing requires review. Novelty against original study unresolved.

priors.claim: A public ranking affects all participant ranks and anonymity settings uniformly
priors.support: Felkey, Dziadula and Chiang (2023) randomly allocate 400 students into teams up to 10; paper reports high-rank motivation and lower-ranked male disengagement when usernames are non-anonymous. The AEA page links OpenICPSR replication E189681V1, whose public catalog shows 496.7KB Stata .dta and 6.7KB .do.
priors.limits: Association of post-treatment rank with subsequent engagement is not randomized rank assignment. Source files not downloaded; user-level data rights, de-identification, assignment roster and eligibility still require review. Product avatar alias may not confer actual anonymity.

priors.claim: A smaller local leaderboard automatically eliminates ranking drawbacks and all welfare trade-offs
priors.support: Chen, Dobrescu, Foster and Motta (2024), Labour Economics 90:102602, RCT of 890 students comparing local rank + goals versus goals/no feedback; local leagues groups up to 30 showed heterogeneous positive effort/grades and negative stress/wellbeing or grade trade-offs. Authors explicitly state no permission to share data.
priors.limits: No original data access; published RCT in university classes not PFL. Local league is not a universal product-safe treatment; must define outcomes including unintended effort allocation.

priors.claim: Leaderboards uniquely increase app participation relative to other salient feedback
priors.support: Karabiber & Gurol (2026), Acta Psychologica 266:106908, online experiment six conditions with N=219 analyzed participants. Authors report leaderboard and progress bar both improved weighted contributions versus no gamification; longer session duration only in leaderboard condition, no significant structure main effect/interaction.
priors.limits: Population ages 18–50 short-term app context not PFL, conditional analytic sample excludes <1 min sessions, 13 excluded arms not specified. Reported significance is authors' result, not reproduced. OSF data link noted but files not accessed.

priors.claim: 5.6% overall short-session exclusions are by themselves sufficient to bound any per-arm retention difference near 5.6 percentage points
priors.support: Published Karabiber & Gurol 2026 includes arm sizes [36,37,36,36,37,37], total N219 and excludes 13 <1-min registrants; independent exact rational enumeration of C(18,5)=8568 possible six-arm allocations gives upper feasible retention difference 13/49=26.5306 percentage points if all 13 excluded had been allocated to a 36-person included arm, while pooled 13/232=5.60345%.
priors.limits: Conditional feasibility, NOT observed dropout pattern, causal bias, exclusion actual treatment assignment, effect on behavioral outcome, external verification or novel 1/3 discovery. If any excluded individuals were never assigned to an arm, 232 is not verified randomization population.

priors.claim: Individual-level 2×2 factor contrasts are invariant to small-room versus large-room weighting and valid under mixed assignments within a shared ranking room
priors.support: Pre-frozen eight group fixture 16 fictitious members in 4 arms: control 0/1 and 3/3 across room sizes 1,3; transparency 1/1 and 0/3; leaderboard 0/4; both 4/4. Equal-room transparency-factor contrast 0.5 vs person-weighted 0.25; tests fail closed on mixed treatment room and non-unique participants.
priors.limits: Synthetic arithmetic only; estimands differ and neither is universally correct. Human interference exposure, cluster randomization, sample precision, legal/ethics and real-person response not observed.

priors.claim: Gamification using points or visual theme necessarily reduces longitudinal study attrition
priors.support: Lumsden, Skinner, Coyle, Lawrence and Munafò (2017), randomized three Stop Signal Task variants (nongame/points/theme) among 482 registered; 265 completed mandatory four sessions and entered primary conforming analysis; six optional days yielded log-rank chi-square(2)=3.0 p=.22 and mean-session ANOVA F(2,262)=1.534 p=.21. Points rated more enjoyable but did not convincingly lower attrition.
priors.limits: No leaderboard or rank intervention: points/theme only. The main attrition contrast is on 265 conforming persons, not proof of effect in all 482 registrations; absence of statistical significance does not establish exact equality. Dataset catalog only, NO individual rows downloaded.

priors.claim: As-of leaderboard membership may be reconstructed from the room visible at the end of observation regardless of transfers
priors.support: Frozen offline fixture: 3 fictitious subjects and 4 synthetic display events, member P0 switches A->B on 2026-01-04T00:00:00Z; 9/9 native Node tests require half-open historical membership to classify each event and reject stale room, overlap/gaps, different arms simultaneously assigned to a room and forged data labels.
priors.limits: Not independently observed event exposure or randomization, not a novel leaderboard effect, no identifiable human outcomes, no safety of real survey/participants proven.

priors.claim: Leaderboard ranking and trends have no published randomized direct evidence separating position feedback from true performance
priors.support: Pickal et al 2026, five arms N427 (86 high/up,81 high/down,75 low/up,95 low/down,90 no feedback), random fictitious images unrelated to actual performance, outcome mean higher/up interest=3.37, no-feedback=3.00, higher/up competence=3.62, no-feedback=3.12. Authors report motivation main effect F4,340=3.18, p=.014; actual performance effects small/negligible. Motivation measured only once, preregistered longitudinal H5 could not be tested.
priors.limits: Original study is not PFL and uses fabricated rankings with debriefing; no actual real ranking dynamic, long-term retention, real person's political choices or platform adoption. OSF original record linked but inaccessible, no participant rows accessed.

priors.claim: Published motivation group mean contrast is automatically identified for all 427 five-arm randomized sample in Pickal study
priors.support: Published F(4,422) for initial accuracy =427; F(4,340) for motivation denotes 345 cases if standard 5-arm ANOVA; 82 present in five-arm reported total but not in that ANOVA. Published interest means 3.37 higher-up and 3.00 no feedback; over scale 1–5, if 82 outcomes have unknown arm distribution, exact worst-case bounds for full 427 are -1.889767 to +2.192222 under stated assumptions. Native test repaired after preserved initial 5/7, then 7/7 pass.
priors.limits: Conditional mathematical sensitivity with extreme unobserved scores and no arm-specific exclusions, not observed dropout, not an ITT estimate nor error in original complete-case analysis; published means rounded; 0/3 scientific novelty.

priors.claim: Palikot paper's 4-week active share 9.6/6.5 can be combined without qualification with 12-week story gain and interpreted as leaderboard mechanism
priors.support: Original paper section 3.1: 4wk stories control .146, ITT +.178; section 3.3: active treatment .096 vs control .065 (4wk). At 12wk stories control .395, ITT +.301, active .143 vs .122 (12wk). A pre-frozen exact Fraction decomposition of E[Y]=p*E[Y|A] gives conditional symmetric contributions extensive/intensive .08713/.09087 four-week and .08510/.21590 twelve-week, if active share corresponds to same positive completed-story metric.
priors.limits: Reported ITT adjusted for strata while public activity rates may be raw; rounded, window lengths differ, activity semantics not fully matched; post-treatment active selection prohibits causal component attribution, original effect is bundled competition, not PFL.

priors.claim: Public CC BY data archive alone proves a legally and ethically sound PFL leaderboard replication dataset
priors.support: Regaco 2026 dataset for Matching-to-Sample learning and gamification on Mendeley Data V2 (21 Apr 2026), CC BY 4.0; index lists data_analysis.R, eval_data.csv and mts_data.csv, experiment behavioral psychology rather than confirmed randomized leaderboard assignment.
priors.limits: Only catalogue/rights metadata examined; no data rows downloaded, no match to PFL estimand, no participant-level privacy adjudication. No A–J opened, only new source candidate.

priors.claim: A public leaderboard offered on its own reliably increases all-user platform engagement and has no strong original field experiment rival
priors.support: Kloc, Belo & Li author working paper Oct2024: Dutch high-school exam-preparation app randomized leaderboard offer 2/3 vs none 1/3 at registration, 3,762 eligible users and 108,171 person-days in Table3. Direct offer coefficient for standardized daily active time +0.009(SE0.016), logins +0.008(SE0.006); no statistically discernible engagement effect on five outcomes. Leaderboard placement 3+ days later conditional on continued activity; no full all-registrant ITT verified. Treatment composition high/low similarity between peers was also randomized.
priors.source_version: Author-hosted working paper October 2024, NOT independently verified peer-reviewed final publication
priors.limits: Do not infer equality or all-user result, cannot re-estimate from person-time aggregates. Inside-board peer distance coefficients 0.092 (SE0.012) etc are post-allocation observational associations, not randomized board-offer effects. No participant data downloaded.

priors.claim: Published individual time-of-use contrast +0.009(SE0.016) rules out +0.05SD effects robustly under any choice of a five-outcome inference family
priors.support: Native exact Git-source-matched Python code and 8/8 tests: point estimate +0.009 SE.016 => normal 95% [-.02235942,.04035942], but Bonferroni five simultaneous outcomes 95% [-.03221327,.05021327]; the illustrative +.05 SD threshold is outside first interval but inside second. All five ordinary 95% intervals cross zero.
priors.limits: Post-source-knowledge chosen .05 SD is illustrative, not preregistered before source consultation or domain MCID. Normal/Bonferroni assumption, rounded original b and SE; correlated outcomes make Bonferroni conservative. It is not an equivalence test, new data, external causal replication or statistical power claim.

priors.claim: Only leaderboards bundled with prizes provide published direct experiments on persistence and cognitive performance
priors.support: Lovász et al. 2023, 5,191 individuals randomized into 8=2 leaderboard presence ×4 subjective feedback arms (none, supportive, praise, trash talk) in an online perceptual game. Published table A1 has 644 baseline players mean1.72 plays and 652 leaderboard-alone mean2.01. These are session-conditioned participants who clicked start, not an all-eligible uptake cohort. Study reports heterogeneous performance and persistence by feedback and subgroup. Original published article repository accessible without human microdata.
priors.limits: Do not compare study populations as direct replication of Kloc field cohort; no person-level rows inspected; differences in means without variance and full covariance are not inferential findings. No new A–J opened merely for extracting its existing published means.

priors.claim: More activity or performance from full public rank unambiguously improves participant welfare
priors.support: Zou & Gao (2023), J Econ Behavior & Organization 216:187–220, DOI 10.1016/j.jebo.2023.09.030. Controlled laboratory four-policy rank feedback: none, private rank, partial public top-third, full public. Authors find full public can increase performance while elicited unconditional WTP indicates a welfare cost relative to partial/no announcement; structural model ranks partial public + financial incentives as favorable under its assumptions. They report 47.1% judge full public recognition welfare worsening, but this is their laboratory measure, not an empirical estimate for PFL.
priors.limits: No person-level data accessed; task cognitive lab, not geopolitical probability forecasting. WTP elicitation and model are context dependent. A score from another task cannot be transported to PFL.

priors.claim: Social information that increases mean crowd forecasting accuracy must also reduce aggregate risk
priors.support: Adjodah, Leng, Chong, Krafft, Moro, Pentland (2021), Entropy 23(7):801, DOI 10.3390/e23070801: study of 2037 people, 4634 forecast sets in seven real financial asset rounds with pre/post information exposure, relating social belief updates to mean accuracy and aggregate predictive risk. Source describes a Pareto accuracy-risk frontier, and the Brexit round as contextual finding.
priors.limits: Not a specific randomized PFL rank intervention. Publisher article text says release data but PMC Data Availability Statement says Not applicable; licensing/rows not inspected. Even if paper open CC BY, no authority to process underlying human data inferred.

priors.claim: A truthful Brier score necessarily elicits truthful beliefs even when only the highest-scoring forecaster wins
priors.support: Witkowski, Freeman, Vaughan, Pennock, Krause, Incentive-Compatible Forecasting Competitions, Management Science (online 2022, volume 69 2023), DOI 10.1287/mnsc.2022.4410. Authors prove classic deterministic winner-take-all can incentivize exaggerated beliefs and introduce Event Lotteries Forecasting mechanism with scoped incentive-compatible selection. Our original frozen Fraction formal product audit C04 reproduces exact scoped counterexample: p=.55 rival=.6, report .61 increases deterministic win chance .45→.55 while a quadratic score-lottery has strictly best win chance at p under fixed rival q.
priors.limits: No novel theorem claimed; no existing PFL winner-take-all payout established; two forecasters/single binary event only, not dependent political elections. Product code is standalone audit, not deployed incentive scheme.

priors.claim: Proper score + public ranked forecasting is an untested governance idea for long-term geopolitical tournament
priors.support: Atanasov et al. (published online 2016, Management Science 63(3) 2017), DOI 10.1287/mnsc.2015.2374, 2400+ forecasters over 261 events and two seasons randomized into prediction markets ranked by earnings or prediction polls individually/in teams ranked by Brier. Carefully weighted/calibrated polls performed competitively with markets; study is not randomized public vs private rank visibility per se.
priors.limits: Rank based on Brier among poll arms does not isolate the social exposure or recognition treatment; published summaries only, microdata not accessed.

priors.claim: Peer social information and team competitive ranking must be delivered as an inseparable treatment bundle
priors.support: Chen et al. (first online 2021, Journal Economics & Management Strategy 32(3) 2023) DOI 10.1111/jems.12459: Taiwan university electricity-saving group contest randomizes contest participation, group composition and competitive inter-team and social within-team information; study reports both information types changed relative rank beliefs and effort. Thus PFL must separate social-belief access from rank publicity for a novel causal mechanism claim.
priors.limits: Residential electricity room-hour outcomes are not probabilistic forecasts or direct prediction league engagement, no person-level source data permission inspected.

priors.claim: Private vs public rank recognition is untested in real field settings
priors.support: Rank as an inherent incentive: Evidence from a field experiment (2012), Journal of Public Economics, contrasts no rank vs privately informed ranking vs publicly posted ranking in language-course TOEIC prep. Published abstract reports initial balance and end-test means 604,656,680 respectively.
priors.limits: Not forecasting or PFL, and not enough evidence to separate effects on public welfare or social learning in political questions.
